invariants.rationale: The method only ever returns 'ids', which is allocated via data.asIntArray() or via new int[width * height], and thus is never null.
Both branches where 'ids' is assigned guarantee that it is either data.asIntArray() (which must match the tile area) or new int[width * height].
An int array of length width * height is allocated, which can only succeed if width and height are non-negative.
Methods on 'element' (e.g., get, getString) are called without null checks, so it cannot be null.
Arrays in Java always have non-negative length.
